originality.rationale: The claimed exact norm 27/11, quadratic mass-deficit estimate, and continuous two-torus projective equality class for the symmetric five-character Lee cross were not stated or implied by the inspected close primary or published mathematics. The most plausible same-support result is over F_3^2, where 3-torsion introduces extra sum collisions and yields 9 discrete maximizers and a different sharp constant. The closest nonaliasing five-character published result is a different Ferrers frequency geometry with a different additive collision structure and constant. The full-axis theorem optimizes over a larger support and only gives a non-sharp inequality for the present five modes. Literature absence is not proof of universal novelty; residual risks are disclosed.

value.rationale: The five-point centered Lee cross is the nearest-neighbor Fourier aperture and a natural split quadratic five-point support; its optimal unrestricted L4 synthesis norm is a precise unknown structural invariant with independent extremizer value. The exact ratio 27/11, two phase freedoms and pointwise-sharp quadratic mass-deficit identify frequency interaction and stability, not a routine restatement of the different published Ferrers norm or the ternary aliased conic norm. Finite grids N>=5 have a uniform constant despite aliasing at smaller orders, a relevant structural threshold; the full equality family clarifies optimal simultaneous horizontal/vertical cooperation. This is a complete small natural classification with plausible use as a benchmark for finite Fourier frame and extension calculations, without claiming broad operator implications.
